## Problem
`src/rebar/llm/code_review/detectors.py:196` and
`src/rebar/llm/code_review/bugfix_size_gate.py:413` hardcode a `severity` string
(`"critical"`, `"high"`) directly into a kernel-shaped finding without ever running through
`pass3_decide` (`review_kernel/decide.py`), so these DET-tier findings carry no computed
`validity`/`impact`/`priority`. The epic is migrating every consumer of `severity`
(aggregation ranking, the review-bot comment, the `fail_on_severity` workflow gate) onto
`priority` instead; DET-tier findings need a `priority` value before those consumers can
treat all findings uniformly. Both sites already carry `"decision": "block"` alongside
`severity` -- only a `priority` value needs adding.

`shim.py::_to_common_finding` (a downstream consumer NOT yet migrated to `priority` -- that
migration is a sibling ticket) reads `f.get("severity")` off every blocking/advisory finding
and maps it via `_KERNEL_TO_COMMON_SEVERITY`, falling back to `_SEVERITY_DEFAULT = "medium"`
when the key is absent. Deleting `severity` from these two DET findings NOW, before that
consumer migrates, would silently downgrade an always-block secrets/size-gate finding from
`critical`/`high` to `medium` in the `review_result` shown to a human. This ticket therefore
adds `priority` ALONGSIDE the existing `severity` (expand, not contract) -- the sibling
cleanup ticket (byzantine-spinelike-penguin) removes `severity` last, once every consumer
(this ticket's DET sites included) has something else to read.

## Approach
At each hardcode site, ADD a `priority` float alongside the existing `severity` and
`decision: "block"` keys (neither of which changes): the secrets detector's finding always
blocks, so its priority is pinned above every configured `block_threshold` (`priority: 1.0`);
the bugfix-size-gate's finding is a strong-but-not-maximal signal (`priority: 0.9`). No key is
removed by this ticket.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `detectors.py`'s secrets-detector finding carries a new `priority: 1.0` key; its
  existing `severity: "critical"` and `decision: "block"` keys are unchanged.
- [ ] `bugfix_size_gate.py`'s size-gate finding carries a new `priority: 0.9` key; its
  existing `severity: "high"` and `decision: "block"` keys are unchanged.
- [ ] `pytest tests/unit/test_code_review_ws5.py -k failclosed_match_names_blocking` and
  `pytest tests/unit/test_bugfix_size_gate_ad0d.py -k test_oversized_bug_fix_without_attestation_blocks`
  pass, with a new assertion added for the `priority` key alongside the existing `severity`/
  `decision` assertions (`test_code_review_ws5.py:196` currently asserts only `severity`/
  `decision`; `test_bugfix_size_gate_ad0d.py:240-243` currently asserts only `decision`).
- [ ] `grep -c '"priority": 1.0' src/rebar/llm/code_review/detectors.py` and
  `grep -c '"priority": 0.9' src/rebar/llm/code_review/bugfix_size_gate.py` each print `1`
  (verifying presence, not absence -- `severity` is intentionally retained by this ticket).

## Testing
Tier: in-process unit test against the real detector/gate functions (pure calculation, no
I/O). Oracle: the returned finding dict carries both the new `priority` value and the
unchanged `severity`/`decision` values, asserted exactly. Existing tests
`test_code_review_ws5.py::test_...` (line ~196) and
`test_bugfix_size_gate_ad0d.py::test_oversized_bug_fix_without_attestation_blocks` (line
~240) are the RED oracles to strengthen (add a `priority` assertion; keep the existing
`severity`/`decision` assertions passing as a regression check that expand-contract left them
intact).
